title: Courageous
slide_intent: Teach writers to show courage through an attempt and the obstacles it involves. The act of competing can carry meaning regardless of the result.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can tie its willingness to challenge prejudice to the courage expressed in its Athlete Oath.
demonstration: A swimmer in a yellow cap reaches through the water. The lower-left text connects courage with speaking against prejudice, while a separate oath panel appears at upper right.
practical_value: Use the athlete’s attempt as the lead when the outcome alone would leave out what made the story courageous.

content_islands.name: Photographic example
content_islands.spec: Fill the page with water and place the swimmer’s stroke in the lower-right field. Retain open water around the action.

content_islands.name: Trait heading
content_islands.spec: Set the red Courageous bar at lower left. Give the oath its own white panel at upper right and include its attribution.

content_islands.name: Meaning and expression
content_islands.spec: Place the trait and voice guidance in two columns beneath the red heading, with enough separation from the swimmer for legibility.
